cleaned_text: HDFC Large Cap Fund - Official Scheme Page HDFC Large Cap Fund AMC: HDFC Asset Management Company Limited Category: Large Cap Fund - An open-ended equity scheme predominantly investing in large cap stocks. Fund Type: Open-Ended Equity Scheme Launch Date: November 10, 1994 Plan Options: Direct Plan and Regular Plan, available in Growth and IDCW (Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal) options. Also known as: HDFC Top 100 Fund, HDFC Large Cap Fund Direct Plan Growth Net Asset Value (NAV) & Assets Under Management (AUM) Net Asset Value (NAV): As of June 01, 2026, the Net Asset Value (NAV) for HDFC Large Cap Fund is Rs. 1,105.80 for the Direct Plan and Rs. 985.65 for the Regular Plan. Assets Under Management (AUM): As of April 30, 2026, the Assets Under Management (AUM) for HDFC Large Cap Fund is Rs. 35,780 Crores. NAV History: The NAV of the Direct Plan was Rs. 925.40 on June 01, 2025, Rs. 680.15 on June 01, 2023, and Rs. 410.20 on June 01, 2019. Fund Manager The fund is managed by Mr. Roshi Jain , who has been managing this fund since 2022. He holds a CFA charter and brings a disciplined, research-driven investment approach. He is supported by co-fund manager Mr. Dhruv Muchhal . The fund management team leverages HDFC AMC's proprietary research covering over 400 Indian companies across sectors. Scheme Suitability & Riskometer This product is suitable for investors who are seeking long-term capital appreciation by investing predominantly in equity and equity-related instruments of large-cap companies (top 100 by market capitalization). The riskometer for HDFC Large Cap Fund is classified as Very High . Large-cap funds are generally considered less volatile than mid-cap and small-cap funds. Suitable for investors with a moderate to high risk appetite and an investment horizon of 3-5 years or more. Benchmark The benchmark index for HDFC Large Cap Fund is the Nifty 100 TRI (Total Returns Index). The additional benchmark is the S&P BSE 100 TRI. Previously, the fund was benchmarked against the BSE Sensex. Historical Returns & Performance The following are the historical returns for HDFC Large Cap Fund (Direct Plan) as of May 31, 2026: 1-Year Return: 17.25% (Benchmark Nifty 100 TRI: 16.80%) 3-Year Return (CAGR): 18.90% (Benchmark: 17.50%) 5-Year Return (CAGR): 19.50% (Benchmark: 17.85%) 10-Year Return (CAGR): 15.30% (Benchmark: 14.20%) Since Inception Return (CAGR): 19.80% (Benchmark: 14.90%) Note: Past performance may or may not be sustained in the future. Portfolio Composition & Sector Allocation As of April 30, 2026, the portfolio of HDFC Large Cap Fund holds approximately 45 stocks, with a minimum 80% allocation to large-cap companies. The key sector allocation is as follows: Financial Services & Banking: 32.5% Information Technology: 16.8% Oil, Gas & Energy: 12.2% Consumer Goods (FMCG): 8.5% Automobile: 7.8% Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals: 6.5% Telecom: 5.2% Others: 10.5% Top 5 holdings include: ICICI Bank Ltd (9.8%), HDFC Bank Ltd (8.5%), Reliance Industries Ltd (7.2%), Infosys Ltd (6.5%), and Bharti Airtel Ltd (5.5%). Investment Details & Minimum Amounts Minimum SIP Amount: Rs. 100 per month and in multiples of Re. 1 thereafter. Minimum Initial Investment (Lumpsum): Rs. 100 and in multiples of Re. 1 thereafter. Minimum Additional Purchase: Rs. 100 and in multiples of Re. 1 thereafter. SIP Frequency Options: Monthly, Quarterly, and Weekly SIP options are available. Systematic Transfer Plan (STP): Available with minimum Rs. 500 per installment. Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP): Available with minimum Rs. 500 per installment. Expense Ratio As of April 30, 2026, the Expense Ratio for HDFC Large Cap Fund is as follows: Direct Plan: 1.02% per annum Regular Plan: 1.72% per annum The TER (Total Expense Ratio) is regulated by SEBI based on the fund's AUM. Larger funds typically have lower TERs due to economies of scale. Exit Load Details The exit load structure for HDFC Large Cap Fund is defined as follows: For redemption/switch-out within 1 year (365 days) from the date of allotment: 1.00% of the applicable NAV. For redemption/switch-out after 1 year (365 days) from the date of allotment: Nil . Tax Implications Tax treatment for HDFC Large Cap Fund: Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG): Units sold within 12 months are taxed at 20% (plus applicable surcharge and cess). Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG): Units sold after 12 months — gains exceeding Rs. 1.25 lakh per financial year are taxed at 12.5% (plus applicable surcharge and cess). Dividend (IDCW): Taxable at investor's applicable slab rate. TDS of 10% for dividends exceeding Rs. 5,000 per financial year. STT: Securities Transaction Tax of 0.001% on redemption. SIP Calculator & Wealth Creation A monthly SIP of Rs. 10,000 in the Direct Plan of HDFC Large Cap Fund, started 10 years ago, would have grown to approximately Rs. 26.2 Lakhs (total investment of Rs. 12 Lakhs), representing an annualized return (XIRR) of approximately 16.2%. A monthly SIP of Rs. 5,000 started 5 years ago would have grown to approximately Rs. 4.5 Lakhs (total investment of Rs. 3 Lakhs). Risk Factors Market Risk: Large-cap stocks, while relatively stable, are still subject to market volatility. Concentration Risk: Heavy allocation to banking sector (32.5%) creates sector-specific risk. Regulatory Risk: Changes in government policies and SEBI regulations may impact returns. Global Risk: Global economic events, trade wars, and geopolitical tensions can impact large-cap companies. How to Invest Investors can invest through: HDFC MF website, mobile app, Groww, Zerodha, Kuvera, Paytm Money, authorized distributors, and Demat accounts. Last updated from sources: June 01, 2026.
